messages:
andrea_support: FYI customer ACME reporting increased tail latencies and a billing spike this morning. They say their clients are pinned to eu-central but we see cross-region egress to us-west. Can someone take a look? :thinking:

leila_cs: repro steps from the customer: 1) hit our /v1/generate with model=redwood-open-7b 2) set header `X-Region: eu-central-1` 3) ~10% of requests show 300-800ms extra and sometimes 307 redirects to us-west. They attached timestamps and request IDs.

customer_acme: (posted by Leila) example curl they ran: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Region: eu-central-1" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — we only saw slow ones between 06:12-06:30 UTC.

mike_runtime: thanks, looking at routing logs now. I see these entries for that time range:
```
2026-03-17T06:12:05Z req=rc_9a2 region_pref=eu-central1 routed=eu-central1 queue=0 fallback_allowed=true
2026-03-17T06:12:06Z req=rc_9a3 region_pref=eu-central1 routed=eu-central1 queue=2 fallback_decision=spill_to_best
2026-03-17T06:12:06Z req=rc_9a3 routed=us-west-2 reason=capacity_exhausted latency_ms=540
```
Looks like the routing policy hit a capacity exhaustion and automatic spill-to-best kicked in.

sara_infra: confirming, the regional queue metrics spiked — eu-central GPU utilization hit 98% and queue depth exceeded soft limit, autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough due to pod warmup. We also saw a short flapping where pinned sessions occasionally lost affinity and got routed out-of-region.

andrea_support: customer is seeing 307s and increased egress charges because traffic goes to us-west. They want either strict pinning to eu-central or a clear opt-out for spillover.

jason_billing: note on billing: cross-region egress is billed at inter-region rates and appears on their invoice as AWS egress. We can create an invoice credit if this was an obvious platform behavior, but need root cause first.

mike_runtime: quick note — our current fallback policy is `spill_to_best` for enterprise customers, which prefers lower latency but allows cross-region when local capacity is exhausted. There's also `strict_pin` mode but it can increase error rate when capacity is gone.

leila_cs: the customer specifically said they would prefer `strict_pin` for compliance (data residency). They didn't want spillover.

mike_runtime: reproduce steps I ran: flood test against eu-central pinned tenant header using our loadtool: `loadtool --concurrency 80 --region eu-central-1 --tenant acme`. I saw queue depth grow and then the router emitted `spill_to_best` events. I can share TTLs and router traces.

sara_infra: logs from router-gw (abridged):
```
[router-gw-4] 2026-03-17T06:12:06Z tenant=acme req=rc_9a3 decision=spill_to_best to=us-west-2 score=0.78 reason=regional_capacity_exhausted
[router-gw-4] 2026-03-17T06:12:07Z tenant=acme req=rc_9a7 decision=hold_in_queue queue_pos=3
[router-gw-4] 2026-03-17T06:12:08Z tenant=acme req=rc_9a7 decision=spill_to_best to=us-west-2
```
So there was a back-and-forth queue then spill.

andrea_support: customer also sent sample request-ids: rc_9a3, rc_9a7, rc_9a9. Can someone check traces to validate latency path and any auth token reissue behavior?

mike_runtime: checking trace rc_9a3 -> shows cache warmup on target shard, additional serialization + cross-region TCP adds ~440ms. Token auth fine. No 401s.

jason_billing: if we give them a credit, need a ticket with timeline and confirmation this was platform-triggered. Incident-bot: can you auto-create a support-incident?

incident-bot: Created INCIDENT-2026-1145 (region-routing-spill). Severity P2. Linked to tenant=acme, owner=andrea_support.

sara_infra: immediate mitigation options: 1) set tenant route policy to `strict_pin` (reject with 429 when capacity exhausted) 2) increase reserved pool for tenant on eu-central (manual cap bump) 3) temporary make a soft hold window to delay spill for 10s so KV cache can warm and avoid cross-region. Tradeoffs: 1) will increase 429s, 2) requires capacity commit, 3) may still cause delays.

mike_runtime: I can push a short-term change: `routectl set-policy tenant=acme policy=strict_pin` — that will force local-only until we revert. It will return 429 on overload. Want me to apply?

leila_cs: please apply and ping me so I can coordinate with the customer. They'll accept 429s over cross-region egress.

andrea_support: go ahead, mike. Also capture metrics 30m before/after and confirm no further cross-region routed requests.

mike_runtime: applied at 2026-03-17T06:22:10Z: `routectl set-policy tenant=acme policy=strict_pin --reason "customer request after spill"` — logs show policy applied to router-gw cluster.

sara_infra: confirming from metrics: after 06:22:30 queue depth decreased and no further `routed=us-west-2` for tenant acme in the next 15m window. There were ~14 requests rejected with 429 in that span.

andrea_support: I'll inform customer: we'll offer a one-time invoice credit pending follow-up root cause doc. Leila, can you own customer comms?

leila_cs: on it. I'll send an update and ask if they want permanent strict_pin or prefer a reserved capacity plan.

jason_billing: prepping draft for credit — need incident timeline and numbers (egress bytes to us-west, number of spilled requests). Mike/Sara please attach counts to INCIDENT-2026-1145.

mike_runtime: adding counts to incident: spilled_requests=118 egress_bytes_us_west=1.2GB 

sara_infra: adding infra notes: root cause = rapid queue growth + autoscaler cold start + sticky-session expiry bug (we found a 30s TTL regression that caused some sessions to lose affinity under load). Patch PR ready #4521.

andrea_support: thanks team. Action items: - Mike: confirm spilled counts and attach traces - Sara: deploy patch to sticky-session TTL and monitor - Leila: customer comms + confirm credit preference - Jason: prepare credit draft and wait for final numbers.

customer_acme: thanks for the quick response. We prefer strict pinning until the TTL bug is fixed. Please keep us posted.

andrea_support: noted. We'll keep this thread updated. :white_check_mark:
